description: Where each part's box sits on the map's coarse grid, [column, row]. Everything else the map draws -- box sizes, pin sides, districts, outlines, routes and bundles -- is computed from the model (apps/viewer/map.js; docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md, "The map"). The map is a second drawing of the same model, never a second model.

provenance.authored_by: handoff the_map_draws_the_end_stop_model, 2026-11-16; re-placed tall by handoff the_map_is_portrait_as_jeff_drew_it, 2026-11-17
provenance.arrangement: Tall, after Jeff's sketch of 2026-11-10 (Jeff, 2026-11-17: the one arrangement is portrait, so it fits the Side by side region): three columns by seven rows. The base body is the left column read upward as the hardware stacks -- hub, tangential link mount, gas-spring mount, piston cover; the pitch plate body the right column in the same sense -- pitch plate, piston body, lower head, upper head -- so the end-stop route runs across the top and the feather stop and the slide cross the middle; the tangential link between its mount and the pitch plate; the pitch link, the pitch arm and the blade down the right below the plate, the hub to blade joint along the bottom. A bearing with no place of its own sits under its link. The pitch plate assembly's members run in a row to the plate's right, two more columns (2026-11-18, handoff the_pitch_plate_is_an_assembly_with_its_bushings): the tangential link's flanged bushing, then the machined plate both attachments' bushings sit in, so the assembly's outline is one row and holds nothing else; the pitch link's flanged bushing has no place and sits under the plate, beside its route to the pitch link; the two straight bushings, top-level parts, sit above the row. Of every placement of the five in those two columns, these three were the only ones the map draws with no route through a box (the other two differ in the tangential link's straight bushing alone); every place of the sketch's arrangement is unchanged.
